shared: The Visigoth is a 60-ton Clan OmniFighter that stands as one of the most widely distributed aerospace designs in the Invading Clans' order of battle. Developed by Clan Jade Falcon scientists and entering production at Complex 9 on Ironhold in 2948, the design struck a balance between firepower, endurance, and structural integrity that allowed it to serve effectively across a broad range of mission profiles. Its appeal to other Clans saw production rights spread through the homeworld factory network during the Late Succession Wars era, and the Visigoth eventually became a fixture in aerospace Stars across all Invading Clans. Though newer designs have emerged as potential successors, the Visigoth's proven record in inter-Clan warfare and the campaigns into the Inner Sphere has made it one of the most recognizable fighters in Clan aerospace inventories.

The Visigoth's fixed airframe is built around a 300-rated XL fusion powerplant that provides the thrust necessary for competitive performance in both atmospheric and space engagements. Ferro-aluminum armor covers the airframe, offering solid protection without sacrificing the structural mass needed for the design's twenty-six tons of pod space. That pod capacity is the foundation of the Visigoth's tactical flexibility, accommodating weapon configurations that range from energy-dominant patrol loadouts to mixed ballistic and missile suites tailored for assault roles. Defensive systems appear across most configurations, with rear-facing weapons a common feature intended to discourage pursuit. The design's heat dissipation characteristics accommodate the heavier energy loadouts without penalty when pilots manage their fire cycles appropriately, though energy-heavy configurations demand discipline during sustained engagements.

The prime configuration combines a large-caliber nose-mounted ballistic weapon with an array of lasers and missiles distributed across nose and wing hardpoints, supported by rear-firing energy weapons that provide rearward coverage. Energy-only configurations replace all ballistic elements with pulse lasers, delivering accurate, sustained fire without ammunition dependency - an advantage that makes them well-suited to extended ground-attack sorties. Forward-heavy configurations push all firepower into the nose and wings, concentrating striking power at the cost of any rearward deterrent. The D configuration exemplifies this approach, combining an autocannon with heavy lasers in a purely offensive armament arrangement that reflects Clan Jade Falcon's aggressive combat doctrine.

The Visigoth's development in 2948 arose from Clan Jade Falcon's need for a medium-weight OmniFighter that could fill multiple roles within a mixed aerospace Star without requiring dedicated specialist frames. Complex 9 on Ironhold was selected as the primary production facility, and the design's initial configurations were validated against the standards of the Golden Century's competitive Trial environment. The soundness of the base chassis encouraged other Clans to pursue access to the design, and Visigoth production spread to homeworld facilities controlled by the Nova Cats, Cloud Cobras, Snow Ravens, Hell's Horses, and Goliath Scorpions during the Late Succession Wars era. This distributed production network ensured the design's availability across Clan aerospace forces even as political fortunes shifted among the Clans over the following century.

The Grand Council vote for Operation REVIVAL in 3048 brought the Visigoth into its most consequential theater. Flying in front-line Stars alongside heavier fighters, the Visigoth performed consistently across the transit corridors and contested aerospace approaches of the invasion. Clan analysts periodically predicted that newer designs would retire it to second-line service, but the pace of the invasion and the steady demand for capable medium fighters kept the Visigoth relevant. By the mid-3050s, the design appeared in the aerospace inventories of every Invading Clan, with estimates placing Visigoth numbers as high as twenty-five percent of individual Clan aerospace forces. This ubiquity drew attention from Inner Sphere intelligence services, whose reports noted that the design's age had done little to diminish its front-line utility.

The Civil War era placed additional strain on Clan aerospace production, but the Visigoth's manufacturing base across multiple homeworld and occupation-zone facilities helped insulate it from the disruptions that affected more centralized designs. Complex 9 on Ironhold continued production through the Civil War period before eventually drawing down its Visigoth line in the Jihad era. The rise of the Jagatai as a heavier and more capable successor design accelerated that transition on Ironhold, though the Jagatai's greater cost and mass left the Visigoth in service across Clans that lacked the production infrastructure for the newer frame. The Visigoth's longevity (front-line service spanning more than a century) stands as testimony to the quality of its foundational engineering.

shared: The Xerxes is an 85-ton heavy aerospace fighter developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar and first produced in 2827 at Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3 on the Kerensky Cluster world of Kirin. Built to embody the Jaguars' direct and aggressive approach to combat, the design prioritizes destructive firepower and durable protection rather than speed or tactical flexibility. Its armament centers on a pair of wing-mounted heavy autocannons backed by nose-mounted extended range lasers, making the Xerxes effective in both air superiority engagements and ground attack roles. This combination of capability quickly established it as a valued asset across the toumans of virtually every Clan. Though second-line designs often struggle to find purpose after the introduction of OmniFighter technology, the Xerxes has remained in active service, continuing to fill escort and close support roles well into the modern era.

The Xerxes is built around a pair of Aero-Model 4 Ultra Autocannon/20s, one mounted in each wing. Capable of firing in rapid-fire mode, these weapons can strip armor from an opposing fighter or ground vehicle in a single pass. Four tons of reloads provide enough ammunition for a typical Clan sortie, though pilots who expend ammunition carelessly may find themselves reliant solely on backup weapons before the engagement ends. Two Series S6a Extended Range Large Lasers mounted in the nose supplement the autocannons at range and provide reliable firepower during strafing runs. The fighter carries nine tons of Compound XAS ferro-aluminum armor, which gives it exceptional endurance for its weight class and allows it to absorb multiple hits during sustained engagements. Its 340-rated Standard fusion engine delivers a respectable acceleration of 3 Gs.

The primary tactical limitation of the design is thermal management. The twelve double heat sinks cannot handle simultaneous fire from all weapons, and pilots who attempt to do so risk an early combat shutdown and complete loss of control. Experienced pilots learn to stagger their weapons fire, keeping heat levels manageable and using the autocannons sparingly to conserve ammunition. The Xerxes is not agile by Clan fighter standards, but its raw stopping power and durable construction make it effective across a broad range of tactical situations.

Developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar in 2827 and produced at Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3 on the shared Kerensky Cluster world of Kirin, the Xerxes reflects the Jaguars' uncompromising combat philosophy from its earliest days. Its blunt effectiveness quickly earned it a place in the toumans of every Clan, and for decades it served as a frontline heavy fighter across both the Pentagon Worlds and the broader Kerensky Cluster. Pilots across the Clans, while rarely questioning its effectiveness, were less generous about its handling characteristics, and the fighter acquired the derisive nickname "Hunchback IIC of the skies" — a commentary on both its ungainly profile and its reliance on brute force over finesse.

The rise of OmniFighter technology during the Clan Golden Century gradually pushed the Xerxes from front-line service into second-line assignments, primarily as DropShip and WarShip escorts. Production at Kirin wound down as newer designs took priority, though the fighter remained common enough that it continued to see action across the Clan homeworlds. Several other production sites, including facilities operated by the Fire Mandrills and Ice Hellions on their respective homeworlds, produced the design throughout the Succession Wars period, ensuring it remained available to virtually all Clans.

Kirin was a world shared between Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Hell's Horses, a co-habitation marked by frequent Trials and little goodwill between the two Clans. When Operation BULLDOG drew the Jaguar Touman away from Kirin in the late 3050s to defend Huntress from the advancing SLDF, the Hell's Horses moved quickly to claim the abandoned Jaguar facilities. The SJ-3 orbital works proved the most valuable prize, providing the Horses with a functioning production line that had already served as the Xerxes' primary manufacturing center for over two centuries. The Horses consolidated their hold on the entire Kirin system even before the outcome of the Huntress campaign was known, ensuring the Xerxes production line would survive Clan Smoke Jaguar's annihilation. The Fire Mandrills and Snow Ravens maintained significant concentrations of the type from stock acquired through Trials and trade, but the Hell's Horses became the design's foremost operator and developer.

During the Wars of Reaving, the Hell's Horses transferred their Kirin holdings, including Orbital Works SJ-3, to Clan Coyote as part of their preparations for migrating to the Inner Sphere. This transfer gave the Coyotes a continuing production capability for the design well into the Dark Age period. The Hell's Horses, meanwhile, established new production at Csesztreg Industriplex Delta in their Inner Sphere territory, allowing them to maintain domestic aerospace manufacturing capacity alongside the variants they developed during their years as the design's primary homeworld producer.

shared: When the Star League Defense Force issued requirements for a new light aerospace fighter in the early 28th century, most manufacturers declined to bid. The challenge called for heavy firepower effective at multiple combat ranges, protection exceeding comparable light designs, and competitive speed - criteria that seemed mutually exclusive at that mass. Blow/Hookson Technologies of New Earth accepted the contract, and in under twenty months produced a flying prototype that met every specification. The Zero entered service in 2703 as one of the finest light fighters of the Star League era, earning a reputation for reliability and combat effectiveness that endured for generations. Its distinctive forward-mounted wing configuration (designed to shield the pilot and engine cooling systems from ground fire) became one of the most recognizable silhouettes in aerospace history.

The Zero's armament pairs a Holly LRM-10 for standoff engagement with two Blow/Hookson Technologies laser systems: the Blow Mark III large laser and the Blow Mark II medium laser. The Mark III features an adjustable focus beam operable in flight, ranging from a wide-angle burst that disrupts enemy targeting electronics to a precisely focused armor-penetrating strike. The Mark II and comparable lasers can only be adjusted by ground crew and are typically set for maximum coherence. Ten single heat sinks manage the weapons' combined thermal load adequately, though pilots running all three systems simultaneously must remain disciplined about heat buildup.

The Bangkock 140 fusion engine provides strong acceleration for the type's thirty-five-ton mass. The wing assembly mounts ahead of the cockpit alongside the engine cooling systems, providing meaningful shielding against ground fire during assault runs. The wings can fold rearward to save hangar space, and in atmosphere allow for an acceleration burst in a dive or a controlled atmospheric skip when deployed at the interface. Ten tons of SlabPanzer V standard armor protects the airframe.

The Zero's principal weakness is its dispersed fuel system: five separate tanks connect through a network of fuel lines, and battle damage to any connection can drain the fighter's reserves rapidly. Pilots must remain alert to this vulnerability throughout sustained engagements.

When Blow/Hookson Technologies of New Earth accepted the SLDF's light fighter contract in the early 28th century, most of the aerospace industry had already declined to bid. The stated requirements (firepower effective at all ranges, above-average armor, and competitive speed in a light airframe) seemed to demand contradictory compromises, and most manufacturers concluded the mathematics could not work. Blow/Hookson disagreed. Their design team produced a flying prototype in under twenty months, and the Zero entered SLDF service in 2703 as one of the most capable light fighters the Defense Force had ever commissioned.

The new design did not wait long for its first test. Later that same year, SLDF elements responded to Rim Worlds Republic forces conducting covert raids along the Capellan and Federated Suns borders, striking civilian targets on New Roland under false identities. General Gaffa Pardoe's Third RCT engaged the raiders, who fielded WarShips including a Dart-class cruiser. Zero fighters executed a sweeping flank while Pardoe's capital ships held the enemy's attention, tearing through the formation and destroying the flagship. The raider force broke and fled, and the Rim Worlds Republic immediately disavowed the entire incident. The Zero had announced itself in decisive fashion.

Impressed by the fighter's performance, the SLDF fielded the Zero across a wide range of commands through the Star League era. In 2707, a variant entered production for SLDF Royal units, replacing the original weapons with a pulse laser battery, upgrading to double heat sinks, fitting a lighter XL engine for improved acceleration, and adopting ferro-aluminum armor for greater protection. The Zero had grown into a family of designs, with its most capable examples reserved for the SLDF's elite formations.

The Succession Wars destroyed Blow/Hookson's production base. The New Earth facility was burned out in 2775, and with the factory went new production capacity. As the decades of attrition ground down Star League-era equipment across the Inner Sphere, the Zero gradually disappeared from the arsenals of the Successor States. By the mid-Succession Wars, the design had effectively vanished from any force not backed by ComStar's technological preservation program. It was ComStar's maintenance of surviving examples on Terra, serviced across the centuries, that kept the Zero from extinction entirely.

At the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, ComStar's maintained fighters faced Clan aerospace forces and demonstrated the enduring value of the design. The Zero's effectiveness against Clan OmniFighter formations (aircraft from a tradition that had evolved independently for over a century) vindicated ComStar's investment in the older type. That outcome spurred ComStar technicians to develop an upgraded variant in 3055, replacing the original missile launcher and large laser with an extended-range PPC and short-range missile launchers, adapting the Zero's engagement profile to match Clan combat methods more closely.

Through the Chaos March conflicts following the formation of the Second Star League, both ComStar and the Word of Blake deployed their Zero forces with effect. Fighter screens proved their worth in brutal actions across the region; at Tall Trees, Zero pilots held open an escape corridor against Blakist aerospace forces, allowing a Com Guards division to withdraw its DropShips against heavily committed opposition. The Word of Blake, which had acquired Zeros through the Schism, deployed the type in their own Chaos March and later Jihad operations.

The Clans had maintained a small number of Zeros through the centuries since the Exodus, treating the type as appropriate equipment for solahma warriors and disreputable second-line formations whose status did not merit access to OmniFighter assets. That the design remained capable enough to serve in those roles after three centuries of service spoke to the fundamental soundness of what Blow/Hookson had built.

Late in the Jihad, ComStar's research program produced a prototype variant, adding a capacitor to the upgrade model's extended-range PPC for increased peak output and replacing its short-range missile launchers with an Enhanced LRM system for greater standoff range. The project was tested several times with positive results before the work came to an abrupt end under unclear circumstances. Whether prototype examples or technical documentation survived the upheaval of the Jihad remained unconfirmed following the war's conclusion.

text.overview: The Vandal is a thirty-ton Clan OmniFighter developed in 2941 by Clan Ice Hellion, conceived from the outset as a high-speed scout and pursuit craft rather than a front-line combatant. Its exceptional agility distinguishes it from heavier fighters of comparable cost, though its limited weapons payload means most Clan commanders assign it to reconnaissance and rear-echelon screening duties rather than direct combat. Every Clan maintains Vandals for fast scouting work, and the design has spread widely through salvage and Trials since its introduction. The years following the Great Refusal gave the craft renewed relevance, particularly among the home Clans, who recognized it as an economical platform for power projection. Clan Hell's Horses became its most committed later-era patron, investing in new production capacity to sustain the type through the Dark Age.
text.capabilities:
The Vandal's defining characteristic is its exceptional thrust-to-weight ratio, which makes it among the most agile fighters in the Clan inventory. Its 360 XL engine provides the acceleration needed to disengage from heavier interceptors that cannot match its pace. The Tokasha Foundry Series 9 ferro-aluminum armor offers adequate protection for a craft of its weight, though pilots who linger in a defensive engagement against dedicated combat fighters do so at considerable risk. The primary configuration mounts an active probe in place of heavier offensive weapons, making the craft an effective sensor platform when operating as the eyes of a Trinary or Cluster. An additional ton of fuel in this configuration gives it superior mission endurance compared to the alternate configurations. The pair of nose-mounted small lasers provides minimal self-defense capability, though aggressive pilots have been known to use them against soft ground targets during reconnaissance passes.

The Vandal's OmniFighter pod system allows rapid reconfiguration between its roles. The tradeoff in each alternate configuration is straightforward: sensor equipment gives way to weapons as the mission emphasis shifts from reconnaissance to attack. None of the configurations are optimized for stand-up dogfighting against comparable Clan fighters; the Vandal's strengths lie in speed, endurance, and surprise rather than raw firepower.
text.deployment: The D configuration appeared in 3063 and found particular favor with Clan Hell's Horses pilots, who appreciate its direct and aggressive weapons philosophy. CHH commands routinely deploy D-configured Vandals alongside Prime reconnaissance elements, using the scouting variant to identify targets and the D to prosecute them. The configuration's straightforward design has been cited by CHH commanders as an example of the pragmatic engineering philosophy they favor, and it remains one of the more common Vandal variants in Hell's Horses toumans through the Dark Age and beyond.
text.battleHistory:
Clan Ice Hellion developed the Vandal in 2941 at the Yoma Aerospace Plant on Babylon, in the Kerensky Cluster. The Ice Hellions' preference for swift, aggressive raiding tactics made a fast light fighter a natural fit for their doctrine, and the design spread to other Clans through Trials and the normal exchange of genetic and technical resources. Within a generation, the Vandal had found a place in virtually every Clan touman, typically filling the scouting and screening roles that larger fighters could not perform as economically.

The Vandal's reputation as a freeborn fighter's craft developed early in its service history. Clan commanders discovered that the threat of assignment to Vandal duty was sufficient to keep undisciplined freeborn pilots in line, and this association suppressed tactical innovation with the design for decades. Few Bloodnamed warriors cared to be seen developing doctrine for what their peers regarded as a punishment posting. This cultural stigma meant the Vandal rarely received the doctrinal attention or logistical priority that designs of its quality deserved.

The Clan Invasion brought Vandals to the Inner Sphere, where they found employment in reconnaissance and pursuit roles that complemented the heavier OmniFighters dominating Clan aerospace assets. Their ability to outrun Inner Sphere conventional fighters gave them genuine tactical value, and several Clans quietly expanded their Vandal inventories without public acknowledgment. The years following the Great Refusal accelerated this reassessment as the home Clans began competing more aggressively for resources and prestige within the Kerensky Cluster.

Clan Hell's Horses emerged as the most vocal advocate for the Vandal's combat capabilities, incorporating the craft into fast-attack operations and forward screening duties that leveraged its speed advantages. The Wars of Reaving and the collapse of Clan Ice Hellion transferred the Babylon production facility to Cloud Cobra control, which continued production through the Dark Age. Clan Hell's Horses subsequently established a second production line at the Csesztreg Industriplex Delta, coming online during the Dark Age to supply their expanding toumans independently. By the ilClan era, the Vandal had largely shed its freeborn stigma and earned genuine respect as a capable scout and pursuit platform.

text.deployment: The A configuration is optimized for air superiority and space-superiority engagements, mounting a nose-mounted PPC flanked by Artemis IV-equipped LRM launchers on each wing. This forward-concentrated armament projects damage across significant range, making the A the preferred configuration for attacking DropShips and contesting aerospace objectives. Its standoff capability renders it particularly effective in transit corridor engagements where closing to short range is impractical, and it is commonly assigned to Stars tasked with escort suppression and fleet defense roles.

The B configuration's four large pulse lasers form an entirely energy-based armament, eliminating ammunition dependency and making the variant ideal for extended patrols and ground-attack sorties where resupply may be unavailable. Accurate at medium range and capable of sustained fire against dispersed targets, the B is a natural choice for ground-attack missions. A single rear-facing short-range missile launcher adds deterrent coverage against pursuit, though pilots must manage heat output carefully during extended firing sequences to avoid performance degradation.

The C configuration mirrors the B's reliance on pulse lasers while adding a rear-facing short-range missile launcher that introduces an ammunition consideration in exchange for improved anti-pursuit capability. Like the B, the C excels in the ground-attack role, and its combined heat load requires fire cycling during sustained engagements. The inclusion of a missile component provides tactical flexibility against pursuing fighters that pure energy configurations lack, at the cost of resupply requirements and the risk of ammunition explosion.

The D configuration embodies the aggressive design philosophy that characterized Clan Jade Falcon aerospace doctrine during the tenure of Khan Pryde. Mounting an autocannon and heavy lasers with no rear-firing weapons of any kind, the D presents an entirely forward-directed offensive posture. This configuration became a common sight in Falcon Stars tasked with assault operations, where its concentrated nose-and-wing armament could be brought to bear with minimal concern for position management. The absence of rearward coverage reflects the Jade Falcon preference for aggressive forward engagement over defensive coverage.

The E configuration is a Civil War-era refinement of the Visigoth's weapons suite, incorporating updated technology while maintaining the design's established performance envelope. Introduced to address evolving tactical requirements across multiple Invading Clans, the E has seen deployment wherever a capable medium OmniFighter is required but heavier designs are unavailable or tactically inappropriate. Its distribution across several Clans reflects the broad appeal of the Visigoth platform as a foundation for updated configurations.

The Prime configuration serves as the Visigoth's baseline combat loadout, combining a nose-mounted LB 10-X autocannon with a mixed array of lasers and short-range missiles distributed across nose and wing hardpoints. Two rear-mounted extended-range medium lasers provide rearward coverage, complemented by standard defensive systems common to most Visigoth variants. The Prime's balanced armament and dual ammunition modes (standard slug and cluster) make it the most versatile configuration in the Visigoth family and the most frequently encountered variant in front-line Stars of the Invading Clans.

text.overview:
The Vulcan stands as the most celebrated warplane ever fielded by the Rim Worlds Republic. Unable to match the Great Houses in fielding large numbers of BattleMechs, the Republic's leadership made a strategic choice early in the twenty-sixth century: concentrate industrial resources on conventional armor and aerospace power instead. Roe Weapon Systems answered that directive with an 80-ton heavy fighter built around devastating wing-mounted firepower and remarkable atmospheric agility. Introduced in primitive form in 2525 and upgraded to full production standard in 2650, the Vulcan became the centerpiece of Republican aerospace power for more than two centuries.

Production was centered at Roe Weapon Systems' main facility on Apollo, with additional manufacturing spread across other Republic worlds. The design survived the nation that built it, passing into mercenary service, Periphery fleets, and independent operators who recognized a capable and durable heavy fighter when they saw one.
text.capabilities:
The Vulcan's large delta wing gives the craft handling characteristics more typical of a medium fighter than its 80-ton frame would suggest. In atmospheric combat, this translates to the ability to out-maneuver opponents that expected a heavy fighter to be sluggish, a quality that more than once caught Inner Sphere pilots by surprise. The Olympus 240 power plant drives the Type 698 airframe at competitive thrust ratings while leaving enough internal volume for a substantial weapons load.

The Vulcan's primary offensive power rests with a pair of Republic Mk. VII Autocannon/10s mounted in the wings. These weapons can punch through the armor of most contemporary designs, and even modern fighters have proven vulnerable to a sustained burst from both guns. A Firefly Type III large laser fitted to the nose in the 2650 upgrade provides reliable supplemental firepower independent of ammunition supply. A Blue Steel SRM-6 launcher and a pair of Firefly Type II medium lasers, one of which covers the aft arc, round out the armament suite.

The design's most significant tactical liability is its limited ammunition capacity. With only one ton of ammunition per autocannon, pilots who spend freely in early engagement risk exhausting their primary weapons before a fight concludes. Effective Vulcan pilots learn to manage their fire carefully, leaning on the laser armament in extended engagements. Republic UltraWeave armor provides solid protection throughout the airframe, and the design's structural integrity allows it to absorb considerable punishment.
text.deployment: The VLC-6N arose as a field upgrade developed by RWR forces in the Terran Hegemony following the Republic's collapse in 2767, replacing the wing-mounted autocannons with Gauss rifles and expanded ammunition capacity. The conversion addressed the original design's primary vulnerability in extended engagements by trading heavy kinetic firepower for greater magazine endurance. These converted fighters dispersed widely through mercenary networks after the Succession Wars began, and surviving examples eventually accumulated in enough numbers to warrant organized refit efforts. A revival of the configuration during the Jihad era brought the VLC-6N back to limited active service among independent and mercenary operators who found the modification as relevant in the thirty-first century as it had been in the twenty-eighth.
text.battleHistory:
The Vulcan's origins trace to the Republic's recognition in the early twenty-fifth century that the industrial gap between the Rim Worlds and the major Inner Sphere powers was too wide to close through BattleMech production alone. Roe Weapon Systems began development of a heavy aerospace platform in the early 2520s, producing the first primitive prototypes by 2525. These early fighters carried twin autocannons and a modest laser suite using primitive technology throughout, including cockpit and engine systems that would be significantly improved in the production variant that followed.

The fighter entered full production as the VLC-5N in 2650, incorporating a nose-mounted large laser alongside improved heat management. This upgraded version served as the backbone of Republican aerospace power for over a century, proving its worth during the Reunification War when Lyran Twenty-Fifth Skye Rangers discovered over Black Earth that their lighter Lucifers were being out-maneuvered in atmosphere by the heavier craft. The Republic's fighter arm continued to make the Lyran Expeditionary Force pay for every advance throughout the campaign.

Following the Star League's seizure of the Rim Worlds in 2767, Roe Weapon Systems did not simply cease operations. Production continued covertly, with fighters quietly distributed to friendly Periphery nations, including 'rebel' factions within the Taurian Concordat. The leaders of the Republic's ruling house viewed anything that caused trouble for the Star League and the Terran Hegemony as a worthwhile investment, and the Vulcan's wide distribution across the Periphery contributed materially to the political conditions surrounding the Amaris coup. After the Republic's eventual collapse following the coup's failure, many Republican pilots took their fighters and entered mercenary service, making the Vulcan a common sight in independent aerospace wings throughout the Periphery.

The design remained active in Deep Periphery hands well into the Succession Wars era and beyond. ComStar confirmed that the Hanseatic League maintained substantial Vulcan fleets, and examples of the design have been observed operating under both Umayyad and Castilian colors. By the mid-thirty-first century the original production lines were long gone, but surviving airframes remained in service across a surprisingly wide geographic range. A student restoration project at Greenock Flight Academy on Firgrove eventually grew into a full modernization effort, and the resulting upgraded variant prompted several small manufacturers to resume production of the Vulcan for the first time in generations.

text.deployment: The Xerxes saw widespread deployment across virtually every Clan touman in its heyday, typically operating in dual roles as an air superiority fighter and ground attack platform. In Points of two, Xerxes pairs mounted coordinated passes capable of challenging even heavily armored DropShips, tearing open armor sections in fast attack runs so that supporting fighters could exploit the damage. By the Clan Invasion era the design had been largely displaced to second-line formations, where it continued to serve as DropShip and WarShip escort. The highest concentrations by far remained with Clan Hell's Horses, who inherited the design's primary production following their seizure of Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3, with the Fire Mandrills and Snow Ravens maintaining the next most significant stocks.

The Xerxes 2 represents Clan Hell's Horses' reinterpretation of the airframe following their consolidation of Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3. Replacing the wing-mounted autocannons with Thunderstroke 2b Gauss rifles, the variant trades the extreme close-range firepower of the base model for improved long-range performance and substantially reduced dependence on ammunition resupply. With 32 rounds available, pilots can sustain engagements over longer periods without the resupply pressure that limits base model operations. The Xerxes 2 is the preferred Hell's Horses variant and is produced at both Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3 and Csesztreg Industriplex Delta in the Inner Sphere, ensuring broad availability within Hell's Horses aerospace forces.

The Xerxes 3 takes the airframe's firepower philosophy to its logical extreme, stripping the design down to a pair of HAG/40 hyper-assault Gauss rifles and shedding supplementary weapons and heat sinks to accommodate them. The resulting configuration delivers concentrated volleys at extended range while eliminating the heat management demands that constrain the base model in sustained engagements. Produced at Kirin Orbital Works SJ-3, the Xerxes 3 is assigned where ammunition resupply can be reliably maintained, and represents the most technologically demanding variant in the Xerxes family.

Introduced as the baseline Zero entering SLDF service, the ZRO-114 was first assigned to front-line formations including the Nineteenth Striker Regiment in late 2703. The design served across SLDF commands through the Star League era, distributed to both standard and Royal units prior to the introduction of later variants. Following the loss of new production, surviving ZRO-114s passed primarily into ComStar's inventory, where they were maintained alongside later variants through the Clan Invasion period. The Clans also retained a small number for use by solahma units and disreputable second-line formations.

text.overview: When the Star League Defense Force issued requirements for a new light aerospace fighter in the early 28th century, most manufacturers declined to bid. The challenge called for heavy firepower effective at multiple combat ranges, protection exceeding comparable light designs, and competitive speed, criteria that seemed mutually exclusive at that mass. Blow/Hookson Technologies of New Earth accepted the contract, and in under twenty months produced a flying prototype that met every specification. The Zero entered service in 2703 as one of the finest light fighters of the Star League era, earning a reputation for reliability and combat effectiveness that endured for generations. Its distinctive forward-mounted wing configuration (designed to shield the pilot and engine cooling systems from ground fire) became one of the most recognizable silhouettes in aerospace history.
text.deployment: Developed by ComStar and introduced in 3055, the ZRO-115 served as the primary operational upgrade for Com Guard aerospace forces through the Clan Invasion, Chaos March conflicts, and the early Jihad period. Its extended-range PPC and Streak launchers were specifically suited to engaging Clan equipment at standoff ranges while reducing the risk of ammunition exhaustion during prolonged operations. The Word of Blake also deployed the variant following the Schism, and ZRO-115s appeared on both sides of the Chaos March fighting. The design remained active in Blakist and former-ComStar forces through the Jihad and into the early Dark Age.

text.deployment: Developed for SLDF Royal commands, the ZRO-116b served as the elite variant of the Zero family during the Star League era, with distribution restricted to units afforded Royal command access to advanced technology. The pulse laser battery and improved powerplant made it a substantially more demanding opponent than the baseline model, while the upgrade to ferro-aluminum armor increased survivability against the weapons common to the period. After surviving the Succession Wars in ComStar custody, the ZRO-116b remained in service with Com Guard units alongside other variants, its Royal command origins making it among the more prized examples in ComStar's aerospace inventory.

A prototype developed during the Jihad at an undisclosed ComStar facility, the ZRO-CX-3 was tested several times with positive results before the program was terminated following the death of the supervising engineer. The variant never entered production, and its operational record consists entirely of prototype evaluations conducted by ComStar. Whether any examples survived the Jihad or passed into wider service is not confirmed in available sources.
